title: Chinese New Year 2027 Greetings: What to Say to Colleagues, Clients and In-laws
description: What to write to Chinese colleagues, clients and a partner's parents for Chinese New Year 2027 (6 February, Year of the Goat): WeChat messages, emails and spoken greetings with pinyin, HSK levels and what not to say.
h1: Chinese New Year 2027 greetings for colleagues, clients and in-laws
lede: Short, natural greetings for the people you actually need to message: a coworker on WeChat, a client by email, your partner's parents at the door. Each one has pinyin, English and the HSK level of its words.

paras: Chinese New Year 2027 falls on Saturday 6 February 2027, the start of the Year of the Goat (羊年, also called the Year of the Sheep).

New Year's Eve, 除夕 (chúxī), is Friday 5 February. That evening is when most greetings are sent. For work contacts, send yours on the last working day before the holiday, before people go home. Greetings are still welcome up to the Lantern Festival, 元宵节 (Yuánxiāo Jié), on 20 February.

sections.h2: The one greeting that always works
paras: If you only learn one line, learn the first one. It is right for anyone, in writing or out loud.

examples.en: Happy New Year!
Happy New Year! (more common when you say it face to face)
Happy Spring Festival!

paras: With coworkers at your own level, use 你. Start with their name: a greeting with a name reads as written for them, while a long forwarded poem reads as sent to everyone.

examples.zh: 祝你新年快乐，工作顺利！
examples.py: Zhù nǐ xīnnián kuàilè, gōngzuò shùnlì!
examples.en: Happy New Year, and may work go smoothly for you!

examples.zh: 祝你和家人新年快乐，身体健康！
examples.py: Zhù nǐ hé jiārén xīnnián kuàilè, shēntǐ jiànkāng!
examples.en: Happy New Year to you and your family, and good health!

examples.zh: 新的一年，我们一起加油！
examples.py: Xīn de yì nián, wǒmen yìqǐ jiāyóu!
examples.en: Here's to a great new year working together!

sections.h2: To clients and business partners (email or WeChat)
paras: Use 您, the polite "you", and address the person by surname and title: 王总 for a senior manager or company head named Wang, 李经理 for Manager Li.

A good business greeting does three things: wishes them well, thanks them for the past year, and looks forward to the next one. For an email, a subject line such as 新春快乐 followed by your company name is enough.

examples.zh: 王总，新春快乐！感谢您过去一年的支持，期待新的一年继续合作！
examples.py: Wáng zǒng, xīnchūn kuàilè! Gǎnxiè nín guòqù yì nián de zhīchí, qīdài xīn de yì nián jìxù hézuò!
examples.en: Happy Spring Festival, Mr Wang! Thank you for your support this past year. We look forward to working with you again in the new year.

examples.zh: 祝您新年快乐，万事如意！
examples.py: Zhù nín xīnnián kuàilè, wànshì rúyì!
examples.en: Wishing you a happy New Year, and may everything go as you wish!

examples.zh: 祝您和家人新春快乐，阖家幸福！
examples.py: Zhù nín hé jiārén xīnchūn kuàilè, héjiā xìngfú!
examples.en: Happy Spring Festival to you and your family, and happiness to your whole household!

paras: Before marriage, call your partner's parents 叔叔 (shūshu, uncle) and 阿姨 (āyí, auntie). After the wedding, most people switch to 爸 and 妈.
For older people, wish them health first. Money wishes are for friends and colleagues.

examples.en: Happy New Year, Uncle and Auntie!
I've come to wish you a happy New Year! (said when you arrive for a New Year visit)

examples.zh: 祝您身体健康，万事如意！
examples.py: Zhù nín shēntǐ jiànkāng, wànshì rúyì!
examples.en: Wishing you good health, and may everything go as you wish!

sections.h2: Red envelopes and the Year of the Goat
paras: Red envelopes (红包, hóngbāo) hold money for children, unmarried younger relatives, and sometimes staff. Use new notes and an even amount; 6 and 8 are lucky, and 4 is avoided because 四 sounds like 死 (death). On WeChat you can send a digital red envelope with a short greeting as its message.
三羊开泰 plays on the old saying 三阳开泰, "spring returns and good fortune begins", swapping 阳 (sun) for its sound-alike 羊 (goat). It only fits a Goat year, so 2027 is the time to use it.

examples.en: Wishing you prosperity! (the classic line when giving or receiving a red envelope)
Wishing you prosperity, now hand over the red envelope! (a joke children and close friends make)
Great luck in the Year of the Goat!

examples.py: Sān yáng kāi tài, xīnnián dàjí!
examples.en: May the Goat year bring good fortune, and great luck in the New Year!

paras: When someone greets you first, thank them and send the wish back.

examples.py: Xièxie! Yě zhù nǐ xīnnián kuàilè!
examples.en: Thank you! Happy New Year to you too!
You too!
Same to you! (casual, between friends and colleagues)

sections.h2: What not to say or do
paras: Keep New Year talk positive: no mentions of death, illness or bad luck, even as a joke. If something breaks during the holiday, people say the line below to turn it into a good sign, a pun on 岁岁平安 (peace year after year).
Don't give a clock as a gift: 送钟 (give a clock) sounds like 送终 (attend someone's death). Avoid white or black envelopes, which belong to funerals, and amounts with a 4 in them.
Don't forward a long group message to a client or a partner's parents. A short line with their name and title says more.

examples.en: Broken pieces, peace every year! (said when something breaks)
